description: Tool name -> tool kind, per surface. Kinds: read, edit, create, terminal, search, subagent, mcp, web, skill, meta, ask. Unknown tools get kind 'other'.

vscode.source: Copilot SDK engine recordings 2026-10-01 (VS Code 1.140.0, @github/copilot 1.0.89-7); WebFetch, skill, tool_search_tool, task_complete and AskUserQuestion recorded 2026-10-10. The older names (read_file ... runSubagent) come from the B1 recording 2026-09-30; a subagent in a Copilot (SDK) session still uses some of them.
vscode.post_kinds_note: The kinds of tool a PostToolUse call is acted on for (hook speed: `.github/hooks/harness.json` starts the post hook only for these, with the `matcher` that `core/postmatch.py` derives from this file; a test and doctor keep the two the same). read/search/terminal: the knowledge base reads and the call record (commands, paths), the reach of a system; edit/create: the task's writes and the health of a task; subagent: the reviewer's verdict; ask: the question tool's return. A kind not listed (web, skill, meta, mcp, other) has nothing done after it: its PreToolUse row is its whole record.
vscode.copilot_names_note: The names Copilot itself gives its tools (`toolName` of the `hook.start` of a postToolUse in `events.jsonl`, 2026-11-25, 552 sessions: bash, view, edit, create, apply_patch, task, ask_user, rg, glob, grep, ...). A hook `matcher` is a regular expression over THESE names, while the hook payload carries the names above (`Read` for `view`, `Write` for `create`, `Agent` for `task`); the matcher lists both. Used by the matcher only: the gate reads the payload names above.
vscode.unrecorded_note: Edit tools named in VS Code, never recorded here under these names (`apply_patch` reaches the hook as `Edit` with plain text). The gate needs them as 'edit'; their input shapes are read generically (nested filePath, patch headers). `bash`, `PowerShell` and `powershell` are guesses for the terminal tool of a Copilot session on Windows (never recorded there; the permission dialog on macOS shows `bash`), listed so the gate reads their `command` whatever the name. Record them when seen.
